activity.notes: In 1610 Galileo was recalled from Padua to Tuscany and appointed mathematician and philosopher to the Grand Duke of Tuscany. He remained based in the Tuscan grand-ducal sphere through the final decades of his scientific career and died in 1642. ATLAS therefore uses 1610-1642 as the representative Tuscan intellectual-activity phase, rather than claiming an exact uninterrupted court-office term for every year.

sources.title: Galileo Galilei — Museo Galileo
sources.citation_text: Museo Galileo records Galileo's appointment in 1610 as mathematician and philosopher to the Grand Duke of Tuscany and gives his lifespan as 1564-1642.

sources.title: Sidereus Nuncius (1610) — Museo Galileo
sources.citation_text: Museo Galileo explains that Galileo's 1610 discoveries led the Grand Duke of Tuscany to summon him to Florence as First Mathematician and Philosopher to the Court.
